Both trials consisted of the following periods: a screening period, a randomized treatment period (Week 0 through Week 40), and a follow-up period (Week 41 through Week 56).

Both were multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo and active-controlled (EU-sourced ustekinumab), parallel-group, Phase 3 trials evaluating the safety and efficacy of risankizumab for the treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.

indication.text: Treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy

citations.quote: TRADENAME SKYRIZI is an interleukin-23 (b) (4) antagonist indicated for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults.

The available safety and efficacy data support the approval of risankizumab 150 mg for subcutaneous injection for the treatment of adults with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy.

target_moa.text: Humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that selectively binds the p19 subunit of IL-23 and inhibits its interaction with the IL-23 receptor, blocking IL-23-driven inflammatory responses that contribute to plaque psoriasis

citations.quote: Skyrizi (risankizumab) injection for subcutaneous use is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that specifically binds to the p19 protein subunit of the IL-23 cytokine and inhibits its interaction with the IL-23 receptor.
Risankizumab selectively binds to IL-23 p19 and inhibits binding of IL-23 to its receptor. This in turn, inhibits IL-23 inflammatory responses that contribute to the pathogenesis of plaque psoriasis.

Risankizumab is a humanized recombinant IgG1 monoclonal antibody that selectively binds to the p19 subunit of human interleukin 23 (IL-23p19) and blocks the interaction of IL-23 with the IL-23 receptor.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥ 1%): upper respiratory infections (13.0% vs 9.7% placebo), headache (3.5% vs 2.0%), fatigue (2.5% vs 1.0%), injection site reactions (1.5% vs 1.0%), and tinea infections (1.1% vs 0.3%). Infections occurred in 22.1% of SKYRIZI vs 14.7% of placebo through 16 weeks.
